purpose: Cited source listing for every deterministic sentence-slop signal. The analyzer and the report-prose linter must not emit a code that is absent here. Signals are leads, never verdicts, and never authorship claims.

signals.meaning: Sentence lengths cluster so tightly the prose acquires a metronome.
signals.false_positive_guard: Uniform cadence is legitimate in reference tables, stepwise instructions, and legal boilerplate.

signals.meaning: Consecutive sentences reuse the same opening frame.
signals.false_positive_guard: Parallel structure that clarifies a comparison or teaching sequence is legitimate.

signals.meaning: Staccato runs of very short sentences used as emphasis filler.
signals.false_positive_guard: Alerts, warnings, and recovery steps legitimately use short imperative sentences.

signals.meaning: Questions posed and answered as scaffolding rather than information.
Stock frames (not just X but Y; whether A or B) carrying no product specifics.
signals.false_positive_guard: A frame instantiated with concrete, checkable content is legitimate.

signals.meaning: Connective tissue (moreover, furthermore, additionally) outweighs content.
signals.false_positive_guard: Legal and academic registers legitimately carry more connectives.

signals.meaning: Paragraphs repeat one internal shape regardless of content.
signals.false_positive_guard: Changelogs and release notes legitimately repeat a shape.

signals.meaning: Favorite phrases recur beyond what the subject requires.
signals.false_positive_guard: Defined terms must repeat; do not flag terminology discipline as slop.

signals.meaning: Prose survives transplant to any product because nothing anchors it.
signals.false_positive_guard: Intentionally generic template text labeled as such is exempt.

signals.meaning: Actors vanish where the reader needs to know who does what.
signals.false_positive_guard: Passive voice is legitimate where the actor is unknown or irrelevant.

signals.meaning: Failure text names the failure but not the way out.
signals.false_positive_guard: Terminal errors with no user remedy cannot offer one.

signals.meaning: A sentence exceeding roughly 35 words asks the reader to hold too many clauses at once.
signals.false_positive_guard: A long sentence that is a single enumerated list with parallel items reads fine; check structure before flagging.

signals.meaning: Semicolon chains or five-plus commas stack clauses into one breath.
signals.false_positive_guard: Citation strings and inline references legitimately carry punctuation density.

signals.meaning: Multiple parentheticals per sentence bury the main clause.
signals.false_positive_guard: A single clarifying parenthetical is normal prose.

signals.meaning: A paragraph beyond roughly 90 words with no list structure becomes a wall.
signals.false_positive_guard: Narrative long-form intentionally sustains longer paragraphs; this signal targets operational surfaces.

signals.meaning: Commitment-free intensity modifiers ('quietly', 'subtly', 'effortlessly') decorate claims that are never made concrete; the word gestures at significance precisely because it commits to nothing.
signals.false_positive_guard: Literal physical uses ('quietly closed the door') and justified emphasis are normal prose; flag only recurring modifiers on unsupported abstract claims.

signals.meaning: A high share of sentences carry short-item rule-of-three lists ('fast, simple, and reliable'), substituting cadence for content.
signals.false_positive_guard: Genuine enumerations, procedures, and legal or safety lists legitimately use threes; only short interchangeable items count, at a four-sentence and 30% floor.
